answer.rationale: Both live problems are funnel-shaped: onboarding completion -4% and activation -6% QoQ. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so simplifying it is the single lever that can plausibly move both, and it targets the durable value of the account rather than its price. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that carried its downside forward intact: +31% signup and +18% revenue against -12pp monthly retention. That is a headline lift masking value destruction, and under a sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective it is disqualifying, not merely risky. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and do nothing for a self-serve funnel that is leaking at the top; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the source of the current decline. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_31 and memory_86 precisely because they are the memories I intend to act on and they are the ones whose summaries read thinnest. Memory_86 says onboarding shortening 'improved completion rates and time-to-value' and memory_31 says cutting required fields produced a 'durable lift' — neither carries magnitudes, sample sizes, or any retention or revenue-quality figure. Memory_73 proves this archive's summaries can retain a counter-signal when one existed, which raises the worry that 31 and 86 were compressed from records where the downstream numbers were never measured rather than measured and found clean. The specific downstream risk is concrete: removing signup fields and shortening onboarding can lift completion by admitting less-qualified accounts and by skipping the steps that create the qualification data and the early habit, converting a real activation gain into a retention or lead-quality loss that would only surface after this quarter. So I want the original records to show whether retention and qualified-revenue were tracked at all, and over what window 'durable' was assessed. I intend a standard experiment with explicit retention and lead-quality guardrails and a holdout, not a broad rollout: the supporting evidence is 45-64 days old, was gathered before the competitor's entry pricing changed the inbound mix, and 'improved activation' is not the same claim as 'improved sustainable revenue.' If verification returns records with no downstream measurement, I will drop to a small guarded test rather than treat the inherited summary as settled, and I will make sure whatever I write back to memory keeps the magnitudes and the guardrail results attached so the next session inherits the caveats rather than another confident one-liner.
